dimension_assessments.summary: Remote identity, degraded UX, mutation/outage visibility, stale-token exclusion, module placement, projections, and lifecycle intent are explicitly stated.
The core identifies offline work, preview-gated remote mutations, diagnostics-only/no-LSP modes, client module capabilities, projection surfaces, and lifecycle supervision limits.
Identity keys and projection fields are named, but normalized mapping inputs/outputs, mutation result semantics, and projection types or invariants are not defined.
Owner, module, and conceptual data contracts exist, but the projection contract and cross-owner dependency representation are incomplete.
Degraded and lifecycle state names are present, but entry signals, mode transitions, state guards, restart flow, and canonical state naming are incomplete or inconsistent.
Remote host/root/session authority, LSPSupport protocol ownership, SSH contract consumption, and exclusion of browser/recovery residue are explicit.
LSPSupport ownership and the external SSH, FileManager, Final GUI, and storage boundaries are explicitly preserved.
Settings, GUI remote-editor surfaces, Search, Source Control, Problems, buffers, and diffs are named as consuming or adjacent surfaces.
User-visible copy, controls, outage modes, preview behavior, and GUI classification are explicit, with stale browser vocabulary excluded.
Connection loss, partial mutation failure, degradation, crash, retry, and restart concepts are present, but their recovery transitions, atomicity, exhaustion, and rollback semantics are incomplete.
Keychain/agent handling is delegated to the SSH owner, but the blind window does not expose the detailed security and privacy contract.
Referenced owner contracts are preserved, but dependency arrays and owner-change propagation gates are absent in the reviewed units.
Retry counts, backoff values, and resource ceilings are named, but enforcement, observability, exceedance handling, and terminal recovery are not operationally defined.
The core states 512MB and 30s limits but does not define metrics, measurement, enforcement, concurrency scope, or platform behavior.

Browser-panel and preview_mode cleanup residue is explicitly classified as compatibility material outside LSPSupport, and legacy local-only session-key wording is preserved as stale context rather than authority.
The supplied gates validate migration and indexing traceability, not executable LSP behavior or failure recovery.

Consequential discretion remains for mapping, retry and offline transitions, workspace-edit failure semantics, projection invariants, lifecycle flow, limit enforcement, dependency propagation, and behavioral tests.
The lifecycle vocabulary is internally inconsistent, several operational semantics are absent, and security adequacy is unknown because the referenced SSH contract is outside this blind window.
